milestones.title: First raid with Artimis
milestones.blurb: Mixed-guild Molten Core — the earliest confirmed raid containing Artimis.

milestones.title: The hunter diary begins
milestones.blurb: Onyxia and an 8/10 Molten Core clear; Artimis starts organizing the hunters.

milestones.title: Ragnaros down, the Choker drops
milestones.blurb: The kill screenshot survives; the neck later fuels the guild's first loot dispute.
milestones.html:
The Choker of the Fire Lord is one of the rarest drops in Molten Core and best-in-slot for every caster and healer in the raid — which made it a test the young guild's loot rules weren't ready for. The policy gave damage casters priority on the neck, on the argument that gearing damage cleared content faster. To the healers, it read differently: the people who kept everyone alive were structurally second in line for the best item they could ever get.

Nobody said much on the night. The resentment surfaced five weeks later, when Deliz — one of the guild's core healers and part of the Nittedal circle — quit the game entirely, naming the treatment of healers and their exclusion from best-in-slot rolls, with the Ragnaros neck as the concrete example. It was the guild's first fairness crisis, and its shape — effort versus optimisation, the meters versus the people who don't appear on them — returned in every loot fight that followed, from the tank-gear debates of spring to the benches of December.

milestones.title: David hands over the guild
milestones.blurb: Discord ownership transfers; Artimis is guild leader in practice.

milestones.title: Deliz quits
milestones.blurb: Criticism of healers and the caster-first Choker policy; he leaves the game the same night.

milestones.blurb: Sleep enters on day one.

milestones.blurb: BWL 8/8 within ten days.

milestones.title: First Rejuvenating Gem
milestones.blurb: Shakey wins the roll the day Fnats steps back.

milestones.title: Glory's first Binding
milestones.blurb: Both Garr and Baron Geddon die four times that night across split runs.

milestones.title: The baby announcement
milestones.blurb: Nefarian dies twice; Anders tells the raid he is expecting a child and promotes Divinestorm on the spot.

milestones.title: Sleep + Ninjas become Dusk

milestones.title: First Dusk AQ40
milestones.blurb: The preparation machine: resistance sets, rerolled professions, consumable pipelines.

milestones.title: The Ninjas bloc departs
milestones.blurb: Nearly the whole ex-Ninjas core raids its last Dusk night; the merger has failed.

milestones.title: GM crisis
milestones.blurb: Yeat transfers guild master mid-conflict; Divinestorm manages it remotely.

milestones.title: Thunderfury
milestones.blurb: Glory's second Binding drops; the legendary is announced the same evening.

milestones.title: Nayla leaves
milestones.blurb: 113 logged sessions; felt unequal to the other tanks.

milestones.title: Dusk enters Naxxramas
milestones.blurb: Three bosses on the first night.
milestones.html: Noth, Anub'Rekhan and Grand Widow Faerlina fell on Dusk's first night in the citadel — but the run convinced the leadership the guild could not clear Naxxramas alone. The internal review afterwards was blunt, and within forty-eight hours the first conversation with Ascension had happened. The Faerlina kill video is the last recording of Dusk raiding as itself.

milestones.title: Joint raid with Ascension
milestones.blurb: Exactly 20 from each guild, picking the strongest players.
milestones.html: Six new bosses died on the first joint evening — Patchwerk, Grobbulus, Gluth, Thaddius, Heigan and Instructor Razuvious — vindicating the partnership overnight and hardening the roster math that had benched twenty people to make it possible. The kill videos from this night carry both guild names in their titles; eleven days later the titles just said Ascension.

milestones.title: Benched — a strike brews
milestones.blurb: Artimis organizes a protest over veterans losing seats; a 37-minute call resolves it the next day.
milestones.html: The Four Horsemen wall — twelve wipes on the Sunday — sharpened everything: who tanked, who healed, and who watched from outside. On the Monday morning Artimis circulated a five-point proposal demanding raiders before members, whole-lockout spots, and collective bench decisions, while the officers held their own open reckoning about the same grievances in parallel. That evening the Horsemen died on the first pull; neither Artimis nor Glory, the two names at the center of the benching debate, was in the kill. The video is the fight from Anders's own vantage point in a later run.

milestones.title: Kel'Thuzad dies
milestones.blurb: Three wipes, then the last boss of vanilla. 43 names.
milestones.html: Sapphiron died at 19:53, Kel'Thuzad at 21:23 — Naxxramas cleared fourteen days after the first joint raid, the goal every December sacrifice had been aimed at. The full stream preserves all three attempts and the kill; the short cut is the celebration version. Within days, several of the people who had stayed for the clear left the game, exactly as they had said they would.

milestones.title: Glory's own Kel'Thuzad
milestones.blurb: Left out of the first kill, the guild's most-attended raider gets his — in the archive's final report.
